name: mminer/consolation
description: A lightweight in-game debug console for Unity that displays Debug output within the game itself, especially useful for mobile platforms where editor logs are inaccessible.
score_rationale: Popular simple Unity debug console with 892 stars that solves a real mobile dev pain point, though superseded by more feature-rich alternatives.
summary: In-game debug console for Unity mobile development

name: ShadowBlip/OpenGamepadUI
description: A free and open-source gamepad-native game launcher and in-game overlay built with Godot 4, featuring input remapping, per-game profiles, and a plugin architecture.
score_rationale: Unique gamepad-first overlay and launcher UI with 807 stars, actively maintained through early 2026 with real hardware integration.
summary: Gamepad-native game launcher and overlay for Godot

name: yankooliveira/uiframework
description: The deVoid UI Framework for Unity providing a flexible UI architecture with navigation history, transition animations, input blocking, and priority-based layering enforcing strict separation of concerns.
score_rationale: Well-architected Unity UI navigation framework with 622 stars, but last updated 2019 making it partially outdated for modern Unity versions.
summary: Flexible UI architecture with navigation history and animations

name: pandr/unity-debug-overlay
description: A fast, garbage-free debug overlay for Unity comprising an on-screen metric overlay, interactive console, and CVar system using format-string rendering without string allocations or mesh generation.
score_rationale: Specialized high-performance Unity debug overlay with 138 stars, notable for its zero-allocation design but limited community adoption.
summary: Zero-allocation debug overlay with metrics and console

name: google/filament
description: Real-time physically based rendering engine for Android, iOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, and WebGL. Designed to be as small and efficient as possible, particularly for mobile.
score_rationale: Google-maintained PBR engine with 19.9k stars, actively used in production (Android Sceneform), supporting all major platforms.
summary: Google PBR rendering engine optimized for mobile

name: bkaradzic/bgfx
description: Cross-platform, graphics API agnostic 'Bring Your Own Engine/Framework' style rendering library supporting Direct3D, Metal, OpenGL, Vulkan, and WebGPU. Used in Unity's Project Tiny.
score_rationale: Industry-standard cross-platform rendering abstraction with 16.9k stars, widely adopted in commercial and indie game development.
summary: Cross-platform graphics abstraction supporting all APIs

name: gfx-rs/wgpu
description: Cross-platform, safe, pure-Rust graphics API implementing the WebGPU standard, running natively on Vulkan, Metal, D3D12, and OpenGL, plus WebAssembly. Core of Firefox and Deno WebGPU.
score_rationale: Essential Rust graphics API with 16.7k stars, integrated into Firefox and Servo, the primary WebGPU implementation for the Rust ecosystem.
summary: Safe Rust WebGPU implementation used by Firefox

name: floooh/sokol
description: Minimal cross-platform standalone C headers for graphics (GL/Metal/D3D11/WebGPU), app windowing, audio, and more. Emphasizes WebAssembly as first-class platform.
score_rationale: Highly popular single-header C graphics library with 9.7k stars, beloved for simplicity and broad platform coverage including web.
summary: Single-header C graphics library with WebAssembly support

name: turanszkij/WickedEngine
description: Open-source 3D engine with modern graphics using DirectX 12, Vulkan, and Metal; supports ray tracing, global illumination, LUA scripting, and runs on Windows, Linux, macOS, and consoles.
score_rationale: Feature-rich modern rendering engine with 6.9k stars, actively maintained with console support and cutting-edge rendering techniques.
summary: Modern 3D engine with ray tracing and global illumination

name: ConfettiFX/The-Forge
description: Cross-platform rendering framework for PC, macOS, iOS, Android, Steam Deck, Xbox, PS4/5, Switch, and Quest; provides building blocks for custom next-gen game engines with ray tracing support.
score_rationale: Professional-grade cross-platform framework with 5.5k stars, used in shipped titles, covering every major gaming platform including consoles.
summary: Professional framework supporting all gaming platforms

name: mosra/magnum
description: Lightweight and modular C++11 graphics middleware for games and data visualization, providing graphics abstraction and platform independence across desktop, mobile, and web with OpenGL/WebGL.
score_rationale: Mature, modular graphics middleware with 5.1k stars and active development (11k+ commits), well-documented for production use.
summary: Lightweight modular graphics middleware with OpenGL/WebGL

name: OGRECave/ogre
description: Object-Oriented Graphics Rendering Engine — a proven, modular C++ renderer supporting Vulkan, Direct3D, and OpenGL with Python, C#, and Java bindings; widely used in robotics (Gazebo, ROS) and games.
score_rationale: Veteran rendering engine with 4.5k stars and 13k+ commits, actively maintained with recent v14.5 release, proven in production across many domains.
summary: Veteran multi-API rendering engine with language bindings

name: DiligentGraphics/DiligentEngine
description: Modern cross-platform low-level graphics library and rendering framework providing a lightweight API abstraction over Direct3D12, Vulkan, Metal, WebGPU, and legacy OpenGL/D3D11.
score_rationale: Solid modern graphics abstraction layer with 4.2k stars, supporting the full range of APIs from legacy to WebGPU with active maintenance.
summary: Modern graphics abstraction supporting legacy to WebGPU

name: Orillusion/orillusion
description: Pure Web3D rendering engine fully built on the WebGPU standard, delivering desktop-level rendering effects in modern browsers with a focus on complex scene support.
score_rationale: Leading WebGPU-native web rendering engine with 5.2k stars, though still in beta and not yet recommended for commercial use.
summary: WebGPU-native 3D engine for browsers in beta

name: LukasBanana/LLGL
description: Low Level Graphics Library — thin abstraction layer for modern graphics APIs including OpenGL, Direct3D, Vulkan, and Metal across desktop and mobile platforms.
score_rationale: Clean, thin multi-API abstraction with 2.6k stars and active development, useful for developers needing portable low-level GPU access.
summary: Thin multi-API graphics abstraction layer

name: patriciogonzalezvivo/lygia
description: Granular, multi-language shader library supporting GLSL, HLSL, Metal, WGSL, and CUDA, designed for performance and flexibility to enable rapid prototyping across game engines and creative tools.
score_rationale: Unique cross-language shader utility library with 3.3k stars, battle-tested across multiple platforms — fills a gap no other shader library covers.
summary: Multi-language shader library supporting GLSL to WGSL

name: KhronosGroup/SPIRV-Cross
description: Practical tool and library for performing reflection on SPIR-V and disassembling it back to GLSL, Metal Shading Language, HLSL, and JSON, supporting all shader stages.
score_rationale: Essential Khronos toolchain component with 2.4k stars, required by nearly every cross-platform graphics pipeline to convert SPIR-V to target shader languages.
summary: Khronos SPIR-V reflection and transpilation tool

name: KhronosGroup/glslang
description: Khronos reference front end for GLSL/ESSL, partial HLSL front end, and a SPIR-V generator; the official compiler/validator used by the Vulkan ecosystem.
score_rationale: Official Khronos GLSL compiler with 3.5k stars, an essential infrastructure tool used by virtually all Vulkan and shader toolchains.
summary: Official Khronos GLSL to SPIR-V compiler

name: google/shaderc
description: Collection of tools and libraries for Vulkan shader compilation, including glslc (GLSL/HLSL to SPIR-V compiler) and libshaderc API; maintained by Google.
score_rationale: Google-maintained shader compilation toolkit with 2.1k stars, widely used as the go-to GLSL-to-SPIR-V compilation pipeline in Vulkan projects.
summary: Google shader compilation toolkit for Vulkan

name: NVIDIAGameWorks/Falcor
description: NVIDIA's real-time rendering research framework supporting DirectX 12 and Vulkan, with ray tracing, render graphs, Python scripting, and DLSS/RTXDI/NRD integration for rapid prototyping.
score_rationale: NVIDIA's professional rendering research framework with 3.1k stars, widely used in academic and industry research for implementing novel rendering techniques.
summary: NVIDIA research framework with ray tracing and DLSS

name: mmp/pbrt-v4
description: Source code for pbrt, the physically-based ray tracer accompanying the 4th edition of 'Physically Based Rendering: From Theory to Implementation', with GPU support via CUDA/OptiX. The canonical PBR reference implementation.
score_rationale: Gold-standard physically based rendering reference alongside the seminal textbook, used in research and industry worldwide.
summary: Canonical physically-based ray tracer reference implementation

name: Themaister/Granite
description: Personal Vulkan renderer with a sophisticated render graph implementation featuring automatic barrier placement, async compute, shader recompilation, and multi-platform support.
score_rationale: Well-regarded Vulkan renderer with 1.9k stars, influential for its render graph design patterns studied and referenced by graphics engineers.
summary: Vulkan renderer with sophisticated render graph system

name: zeux/niagara
description: Vulkan renderer written from scratch on stream, demonstrating modern Vulkan techniques including GPU culling, mesh shading, and occlusion culling without third-party Vulkan libraries.
score_rationale: Educational Vulkan renderer with 1.7k stars from a respected graphics engineer, valuable for learning modern GPU-driven rendering techniques.
summary: Educational Vulkan renderer with GPU culling techniques

name: software-mansion/TypeGPU
description: Modular WebGPU toolkit with advanced TypeScript type inference, allowing developers to write GPU shaders directly in TypeScript with automatic WGSL generation and type-safe buffer management.
score_rationale: Innovative TypeScript-first WebGPU toolkit with 2.3k stars, recently released (v0.10 in 2026) and filling a unique niche for type-safe GPU programming on the web.
summary: TypeScript-first WebGPU toolkit with type-safe shaders

name: appleseedhq/appleseed
description: Modern open source physically-based rendering engine for animation and visual effects, featuring global illumination, spectral rendering, and both C++ and Python APIs. Designed for production VFX workflows.
score_rationale: 2.3k-star production-oriented renderer with professional feature set and VFX industry targeting, though releases slowed after 2019.
summary: Production-grade PBR renderer for animation and VFX

name: KTStephano/StratusGFX
description: Real-time 3D rendering engine with physically-based rendering, real-time global illumination, and modern graphics techniques built on OpenGL 4.6.
score_rationale: Promising hobby research renderer with 801 stars featuring real-time GI, but still in pre-release with known instability on limited platforms.
summary: Real-time 3D engine with global illumination research

name: sezanzeb/input-remapper
description: Easy-to-use Linux tool for remapping input devices including keyboards, mice, gamepads, joysticks, and wheels. Supports X11, Wayland, programmable macros, and is widely used for accessibility adaptations.
score_rationale: Most popular open-source Linux input remapper with 5.5k stars, actively maintained through November 2025, GPL-3.0, and essential for accessibility and gaming input customization.
summary: Linux input remapper for accessibility and gaming

name: AntiMicroX/antimicrox
description: Graphical program to map gamepad/joystick buttons to keyboard, mouse, scripts, and macros on Linux and Windows. Enables controller use in games and apps that lack native gamepad support.
score_rationale: Widely used gamepad-to-keyboard mapper with 3.6k stars, actively maintained through January 2025, GPL-3.0, and the standard tool for playing keyboard-only games with a controller.
summary: Gamepad-to-keyboard mapper for Windows and Linux

name: mdqinc/SDL_GameControllerDB
description: Community-sourced database of game controller mappings for SDL2 and SDL3, providing button/axis mappings for hundreds of controllers across Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, and iOS.
score_rationale: Indispensable SDL controller mapping database with 1.7k stars, continuously updated by the community, and integrated into virtually every SDL-based game for out-of-the-box controller support.
summary: Community controller mapping database for SDL games

name: MarcoFazioRandom/Virtual-Joystick-Godot
description: Simple, customizable virtual joystick plugin for Godot supporting fixed, dynamic, and following modes with configurable dead zones, visibility options, and 2D/3D game compatibility for mobile touchscreen input.
score_rationale: Most starred Godot virtual joystick solution with 949 stars, MIT licensed, and the standard choice for adding mobile touch controls to Godot games.
summary: Virtual joystick plugin for Godot mobile games
